narrative: Semiconductor and AI-related stocks saw steep declines, with LITE, CRDO, MU, AMD, MRVL, and NBIS each falling between 15% and 19% as AI spending fears wiped roughly $2 trillion off the Nasdaq in October. Major strategic shifts are underway across infrastructure: Marvell agreed to acquire Lumentum in a $115 billion deal for AI data center connectivity, Microsoft signed a 20-year power deal with Chevron but declined to expand a separate Texas data center agreement, and Samsung will manufacture AMD and Nvidia chip parts at a new Texas plant. The power and nuclear sectors are accelerating to meet data center demand, with PJM revising procurement rules, a U.S. regulator adopting an interventionist approach to connections, Cameco narrowing its uranium forecast, and Kazakhstan planning a strategic reserve. Meanwhile, Agility Robotics became the first pure-play humanoid robot company to go public in the U.S., and the Pentagon surged over 25,000 drones to CENTCOM while lending Neros $450 million toward a million-unit annual production target.
